schema_note: Every number in this file is real and independently reproducible -- computed from actual sacrebleu runs, actual verification-pipeline state files, or actual dataset files in the lao-thai-translator repo. Nothing here is estimated, projected, or hand-typed as a round number. Fields with a null value mean 'not measured under this methodology,' never 'assumed good.'

generations.label: Generation 3
generations.release_notes: The DPO-trained checkpoint produced by an earlier 5-step sanitization-pipeline retrain. Superseded after we identified what we internally call the 'Generation 3 crisis': a cycle-consistency blind spot where a forward and reverse translation model can share a bias that round-trips cleanly while being confidently wrong about the actual meaning. That specific failure mode is the reason Generation 4's verification system (below) uses back-translation as only one of two independent checks, never the sole gate. We don't show chrF++/BLEU scores for Generation 3 -- it predates this project's current benchmark suites, and we'd rather show nothing than a number we didn't actually measure.

generations.label: Generation 4 (current for "Translated screenplay" files, being replaced)

defect_categories_fixed: Garbled decoder artifact (a bare "ແມ" token left as an incomplete fragment, never finished into a real word)
Repetition / stutter artifacts (e.g. a phrase's opening words duplicated back-to-back)
"Cat" hallucination (a garbled token completed into the unrelated real word for "cat")
"Interfere" hallucination (the real word for "interfere/intervene" substituted for unrelated content -- the single largest defect pattern found in this project)
Code-mixing (untranslated English words left stranded inside otherwise-Lao sentences)
Numeral errors (e.g. "100 thousand" rendered as "ten thousand")

generations.release_notes: The 287 films in the verification run (285 are still published) were re-checked automatically by two machine filters -- no human reviewer read or approved these translations. Filter 1 is a set of deterministic Lao-text pattern checks built and refined by hand as each new failure pattern was found. Filter 2 is an English-only back-translation semantic-equivalence judge -- the model is never shown its own Lao output to grade, precisely because that self-referential check is what caused the Generation 3 crisis. An automatic correction was applied only when both filters independently flagged the same segment. This process applied 7,231 automatic corrections (the figure this page's Model Evolution card had previously shown, 7,251, was a stale snapshot from an earlier point in the catalog -- corrected here to match the current 285-film published catalog). The largest single defect found was a hallucinated substitution of the real Lao word for 'interfere' standing in for unrelated content -- 654 raw occurrences found corpus-wide; a dedicated cleanup pass fixed only 15 of those (2.6%), confirming most instances are a stable model bias rather than a one-off translation slip. That known limitation is left undisturbed in the published corpus rather than papered over, pending a future targeted retrain. Separately, the review step that produced the published files sent lines to Google Gemini, a cloud AI service, and applied some of its edits; that step will not be used again. The model was fine-tuned mostly on machine-translated text, including earlier output of this project and corrections written by Google Gemini; only a small share of its training data was translated by people.

generations.label: Generation 5 (retired plan)
generations.release_notes: This DPO/self-training plan was abandoned; training was never started. The staged dataset numbers below are kept as a historical record only. The next candidate under evaluation is a supervised adapter (S3X), to be checked by a native Lao reader before any use. We publish performance numbers only after they're actually measured against a trained, evaluated checkpoint -- this entry intentionally has no scores yet.

generations.label: S3X (current for "Subtitles" files)
generations.release_notes: S3X is a supervised (non-DPO) LoRA adapter fine-tuned on NLLB-200 1.3B. It is used for every file on this site labeled "Subtitles": real, timed English subtitle files translated directly, with no cloud AI review step (no Google Gemini pass, unlike the older "Translated screenplay" files) and no find-and-replace rule-table post-processing. Files still labeled "Translated screenplay" are Generation 4 output and are being replaced by real subtitle-timed "Subtitles" files as they become available. Like every generation on this page, S3X was fine-tuned mostly on machine-translated text, including earlier output of this project and corrections written by Google Gemini; only a small share of its training data was translated by people -- a fact about training data, not about how S3X's own output is produced or reviewed. No quality score is published for S3X: no native Lao reader has reviewed it yet, and this project does not publish a result before it is actually measured (see the Quality Score section).
